# SpotCheck

> A free toolkit of eight browser bookmarklets and three DevTools extensions for spot-checking web accessibility. Each tool runs entirely client-side against the current page's DOM, requires no installation or extension permissions, and sends nothing to a server. Every tool maps to specific WCAG 2.2 success criteria.

SpotCheck is built and maintained by Homer Gaines, a UI engineer and certified accessibility professional. The tools are dependency-free vanilla JavaScript, and the readable unminified source for each one is published on its page.

Intended use: fast spot-checks during development, code review, and triage. SpotCheck is not a substitute for a full manual audit or for testing with assistive technology. Automated checks catch a minority of accessibility issues, and every tool page states what its check cannot detect.

## Tools

- [Landmark Visualizer](https://www.spotcheck.tools/landmark-visualizer): Outlines every ARIA and HTML landmark region on the page and flags regions that are duplicated or missing an accessible name. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.
- [Link Accessibility Auditor](https://www.spotcheck.tools/link-accessibility-auditor): Checks every link for an accessible name and flags generic text such as "click here" or "read more" that gives no context out of order. Relates to 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) and 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only).
- [Heading Validator](https://www.spotcheck.tools/heading-validator): Walks the heading outline in document order and flags any level that skips ahead, which breaks screen reader navigation by heading. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels.
- [List Identifier](https://www.spotcheck.tools/list-identifier): Flags empty lists, malformed markup, and list items that aren't inside a list at all, which corrupts the item count a screen reader announces. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.
- [Tab Order Visualizer](https://www.spotcheck.tools/tab-order-visualizer): Numbers every focusable element in tab order and flags positive tabindex values that desynchronize focus order from visual order. Relates to 2.4.3 Focus Order and 2.4.7 Focus Visible.
- [Text Contrast Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/text-contrast-checker): Measures text contrast against its effective background and flags anything below the WCAG AA minimum. Relates to 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) and 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced).
- [Alt Text Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/alt-text-checker): Checks every image for alt text and flags the ones missing it or marked incorrectly. Relates to 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
- [Input Label Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/input-label-checker): Outlines every input, select, and textarea on the page and labels each one with how it gets its accessible name. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions, and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

## How to use a bookmarklet

- [SpotCheck home](https://www.spotcheck.tools/): Drag any tool's button to your browser bookmarks bar, navigate to the page you want to test, then click the bookmark. Results are drawn as outlines on the page with a summary panel. Click the bookmark again to clear. Each tool page includes an inline demo you can run without installing anything, and the full source for review.
